paper.title: Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots
paper.abstract: A purely data-driven method grounded in the theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs) was recently used to model and control nonlinear soft robotic simulators. Here, we extend the methodology to learn aSSM-reduced models from data collected from hardware soft robotic platforms. Specifically, we learn a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot. We then use this ODE in a model predictive control scheme to demonstrate real-time precision control across various challenging closed-loop trajectory-tracking tasks, ranging from 2D to 3D trajectories with static and dynamic constraints. We find that our methodology enhances accuracy and precision across all control tasks compared to available data-driven linear methods and model-free reinforcement learning. While we focus here on a soft-helicoid trunk robot, our methodology relies solely on hardware data and is therefore applicable to a broader class of soft robotic systems.

analysis.relevance_note: Soft-robot model reduction and hardware predictive control are the main focus.

paper.title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
paper.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) requires large amounts of interaction data or a reliable simulator, both hard to obtain for nonlinear soft robotic hardware. Recent work shows that a time-scale separation inherent to soft robot dynamics justifies their reduction to low-dimensional invariant manifolds, known as adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs). We demonstrate that an aSSM-reduced model, a simple polynomial ordinary differential equation learned purely from pre-collected data, can serve as an RL training environment. On a pneumatically actuated soft arm, we train a trajectory-tracking policy in 3 hours on a six-dimensional aSSM-reduced model and deploy it without fine-tuning, whereas reproducing this policy training extrapolates to 3 years of hardware interaction. Our policy tracks dynamic targets with 40% lower error than otherwise identical policies trained on a 4.8-million-parameter recurrent neural network (RNN) or a 1.7-million-parameter transformer, which take 13 and 100 hours to identify, against 5 minutes for our mathematically justified 6,924-parameter model.

analysis.relevance_note: Reinforcement-learning acceleration for soft robots is the main focus, without a central profile theme.

paper.title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
paper.abstract: We study the learning of homogenized constitutive laws for inelastic heterogeneous materials, aiming to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations with surrogates that generalize across loading histories and microstructures. We focus on the recurrent neural operator framework, motivated by the explicit form of homogenized Kelvin--Voigt linear viscoelasticity. In this framework, internal variables enable a Markovian approximation of loading-history dependence, and neural operators represent the microstructure-dependent constitutive response. For periodic Kelvin--Voigt viscoelasticity, we prove a universal approximation theorem showing that the model can approximate the homogenized constitutive law to any prescribed accuracy, uniformly in time and over a wide set of admissible strain trajectories and microstructural property fields, in two and three dimensions. This comprises a significant extension of the existing, somewhat limited, one-dimensional theory that uses explicit solutions for piecewise constant materials. Instead, in two and three dimensions, we adopt a more versatile approximation based on the spectral representation of the memory kernel that arises from homogenization. This also enables us to give an explicit bound on the internal-variable dimension, sufficient for approximation, exhibiting logarithmic growth in the inverse relative stress error and in material contrast. Numerical experiments on viscoelasticity and crystal plasticity complement the theory, illustrating the roles of internal-variable dimension and sample complexity in learning homogenized responses from unit-cell data. Theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.

analysis.relevance_note: Constitutive-law approximation and learned homogenization dominate; internal-variable size is approximation complexity, not a fractal invariant.

paper.title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
paper.abstract: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $\Gamma$ to $\Lambda$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.

analysis.tldr: The author claims Mal’cev-completion rigidity for integrably measure-equivalent torsion-free nilpotent groups.

analysis.main_result: For infinite finitely generated torsion-free nilpotent groups, the author claims that integrable measure equivalence forces isomorphic Mal’cev completions, and states the corresponding quasi-isometric rigidity conclusion as resolving the named Gromov conjecture. Applications concern lifting quasi-isometric embeddings and Betti numbers. paper.title: A Finite-Lag Markov Chain Model for Coarse-Graining Linear SDEs
paper.abstract: In this paper, we analyze a finite-lag Markov chain approximation for coarse-grained linear stochastic differential equations. The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of the resolved variables to advance on a prescribed time grid. Its stability and statistical properties are studied, with particular attention to the role of the lag time. The chain preserves the exact equilibrium distribution and matches the autocovariance at the chosen lag, while errors at subsequent times are quantified. For a slow-fast system, the analysis relates lag selection to scale separation and dynamical accuracy. A continuous embedding of the chain enables a unified comparison with some existing continuous-time Markovian effective models based on the temporal statistics they preserve. Numerical examples illustrate the theoretical results.

analysis.relevance_note: Exact equilibrium preservation in reduced stochastic dynamics gives an invariant-measure connection.
analysis.tldr: A finite-lag Markov approximation preserves a linear SDE’s resolved equilibrium law and its autocovariance at the selected lag.
analysis.problem: Understand lag-dependent stability and statistical fidelity of coarse-grained linear stochastic models.
analysis.main_result: The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of resolved variables on a fixed time grid. It preserves the exact equilibrium distribution and matches the chosen-lag autocovariance; later-time errors are quantified. Slow-fast analysis connects lag choice to scale separation and accuracy. A continuous embedding compares preserved temporal statistics with continuous-time Markovian effective models. Exact error bounds are not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
paper.abstract: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.

analysis.relevance_note: Commutation of flows and Lie-algebra structures provide a geometric-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: A law-sensitive Lie bracket characterizes commuting nonlocal flows and supports particle-uniform second-order expansions.
analysis.problem: Extend vector-field commutator calculus to measure-dependent dynamics.
analysis.main_result: Under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions, vanishing of the Lie–Lions bracket is equivalent to commutation of global flows on finite-second-moment probability measures. Complete polynomial nonlocal fields form a Lie algebra and admit commutator and second-order Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formulas with cubic Wasserstein remainders, controlled by the second moment uniformly in particle number. A spatial bracket at a fixed law alone is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation, as collective-dynamics examples show.
analysis.context: Nonlocal flow geometry on probability measures.

paper.title: The balance between feature learning and collapse in dynamical systems-based generative models
paper.abstract: Over the past decade, a growing body of work has established that implicit biases in learning dynamics fundamentally shape the solutions found by neural networks, governing their learned features and generalisation performance. However, despite these strides in deep learning theory, far less is known about representation learning in generative models based on dynamical systems, from normalising flows to diffusion. Importantly, empirical evidence suggests that continuous-time generative models can be prone to mode collapse, yet a learning theory explaining such biases remains elusive. To address this, we use tools from dynamical systems and operator theory to express the gradient flow of a general class of stochastic differential equations as a composition of linear operators, allowing us to relate collapse to low-rank biases in generative models. In variational inference and flow-matching tasks, we show that this bias can manifest in two different mechanisms: i) where collapsed models are stable fixed points of the gradient flow, or ii) in sequential feature learning, where smaller modes take progressively longer to be learned, producing an effective collapse for a fixed training budget. Together these findings point to a trade-off between feature learning and collapse, suggesting an operator view as a step towards a unified framework for understanding the learning dynamics of dynamical systems-based generative models.

analysis.relevance_note: Generative-model training biases and mode collapse dominate, without a central profile theme.

paper.title: Reconstructing Flash-Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain and Tracking Cortical Activity Using Spatiotemporal Filtering: Numerical Simulation Study
paper.abstract: Electroencephalographic source reconstruction of visual evoked activity is challenging because distributed, temporally evolving, and overlapping cortical sources generate scalp potentials. We present a controlled simulation framework for flash visual evoked potentials (FVEPs) based on a coupled Jansen--Rit neural mass network and a realistic finite-element EEG forward model. The framework generates a sequential activation pattern across early visual, parietal, and frontal regions and enables direct comparison of reconstructed activity with known ground truth. Standardized Kalman filtering (SKF), change-rate SKF (CrSKF), conventional Kalman filtering (KF), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) beamforming are compared using parcel-wise time courses, temporal lags, and assessments of spatial focality and Earth Mover's Distance. In the inverse comparison, SKF and CrSKF preserve the principal temporal progression more consistently than KF and LCMV, while CrSKF produces smoother temporal estimates. The results also demonstrate parcel-wise leakage and reduced separation of closely spaced components, emphasizing the need to interpret temporal ordering together with spatial reconstruction quality. The proposed framework provides a reproducible test environment for evaluating dynamic EEG inverse methods under controlled noise conditions.

analysis.relevance_note: Numerical EEG source reconstruction and filtering comparisons are the main focus.

paper.title: Converse Lyapunov theorem for input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems
paper.abstract: We prove converse Lyapunov theorems for input-to-state stability (ISS) of a broad class of infinite-dimensional systems applicable to evolution equations in Banach spaces, boundary control systems, and delay systems. To this end, we employ a novel method that does not require constructing auxiliary closed-loop systems. We start by showing that ISS of a control system implies uniform global asymptotic stability of the same system with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. Then, under an additional regularity requirement, we prove that an ISS Lyapunov function can be constructed. Based on our general result, we prove that for linear systems with unbounded $\infty$-admissible operators, ISS is equivalent to the existence of a Lipschitz continuous coercive ISS Lyapunov function.

analysis.relevance_note: Input-to-state stability and infinite-dimensional control Lyapunov theory dominate.

paper.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations of Space Forms: Curvature Pinching, Soliton Rigidity, Conjugate Loci, and Superintegrability
paper.abstract: We study the one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics $g_\lambda$ induced by the Hamiltonian cotangent deformation $H_\lambda = H_0 + \frac{\lambda}{2}\|J\|^2$ on simply connected space forms of constant curvature $\kappa \in \{1, 0, -1\}$, where $J$ is the momentum map of the isotropy action fixing a base point. The master reciprocal identity $1/f_\lambda^2 = 1/s_\kappa^2 + \lambda$ governing the warping function controls the geometry of the family and implies that radial geodesic acceleration is independent of $\lambda$. From this mechanism we derive three classes of results: (1) Curvature and rigidity: closed-form sectional curvatures, the sharp positivity trichotomy, pointwise and global Brendle-Schoen $1/4$-pinching windows on $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, never-Einstein rigidity for $\lambda \neq 0$, and the realization of Hamilton's steady cigar soliton on $(\mathbb{H}^2, g_1)$ as the unique gradient Ricci soliton in the family. (2) Dynamics and stability: iso-kinematic decoupling into unperturbed radial motion and uniform precession $\Omega = \lambda L$, closed-form Clairaut integration, the transcendental inward conjugate point law with Euclidean inversion $r_0 R^* = 1/\lambda$, and stratified $A_3$ cusp caustics. (3) Integrability and spectral theory: maximal superintegrable rational pericenter invariants on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, transverse Killing rigidity on curved space forms, Fuchsian Heun spectral reduction with modulus $\tau = 1 + \lambda/\kappa$, and essential spectrum gap collapse to $[0, \infty)$ on $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$. Extensions to anisotropic sphere families and intrinsic deformations of compact rank-one symmetric spaces ($\mathbb{C}P^n, \mathbb{H}P^n, \mathbb{O}P^2$) are also established.

analysis.tldr: A Hamiltonian deformation of space forms yields explicit geometric, geodesic and spectral conclusions.

analysis.main_result: For the stated one-parameter deformation on simply connected space forms, the author derives a reciprocal warping identity implying parameter-independent radial acceleration. The abstract claims explicit curvature and pinching results, non-Einstein rigidity away from zero parameter, a unique cigar-soliton realization within the family, radial/precessional geodesic decoupling, conjugate-locus laws and caustics. It also states Euclidean superintegrability and curved-space spectral reductions. Detailed parameter domains of the individual conclusions: Not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations and Closed-Form Geodesics on Non-Naturally Reductive Orbit Spheres: The Spin(9) 15-Sphere and the Cayley Plane
paper.abstract: By the Skew-Torsion Holonomy Theorem of Olmos and Reggiani (2012), the 15-sphere $S^{15}$ admits no non-trivial naturally reductive metric under any transitive Lie group, precluding geodesic integration via canonical Ambrose-Singer connections. Simultaneously, Nikonorov (2013) established that every $Spin(9)$-invariant metric on $S^{15}$ is a geodesic orbit (GO) space. We integrate the geodesic flow on this non-naturally reductive GO manifold via the Lie Subalgebra Closure Principle: whenever the slice generators of a multi-axial reductive decomposition close into a finite-rank reductive Lie subalgebra, the geodesic vector equations decouple into an algebraic eigenvalue problem. Using the 16-dimensional spin representation and Vol'per's decomposition $\mathfrak{spin}(9) = \mathfrak{spin}(7) \oplus \mathfrak{p}_1 \oplus \mathfrak{p}_2$, we prove that the slice generators $X_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_2$ and $Y_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_1$ close into $\mathfrak{u}(2) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1) \subset \mathfrak{so}(16)$. The generator $M = \alpha X_1 + \beta Y_1$ has the four-mode spectrum $\Omega \in \{ |R \pm 3\alpha|, |R \pm \alpha| \}$ ($R = \sqrt{\alpha^2 + \beta^2}$), yielding a closed-form 4-projector decomposition and Euler-Cartan factorization for $\exp(\alpha X_1 + \beta Y_1)$. Under the normalized Ricci flow, we prove that the Bourguignon-Karcher squashed Einstein metric at $t = 3/11$ ($\lambda = 64$) is an unstable repeller separating sub-Riemannian fiber collapse from the round sphere basin. Finally, on the deformed Cayley plane $\mathbb{O}P^2 = F_4/Spin(9)$, we prove universal CROSS never-Einstein rigidity, establish the 15-dimensional three-stratum Whitney stratification of the cut locus $Cut(q_0)$ at non-polar basepoints $q_0$, and prove Blaschke and Besse rigidity for all $\lambda > 0$.

analysis.tldr: Lie-subalgebra closure gives explicit geodesic integration for the stated invariant fifteen-sphere family.
analysis.problem: Integrate invariant geodesic equations through finite-dimensional algebraic closure.
analysis.main_result: Using the spin representation and a reductive decomposition, the author claims that specified slice generators close into a unitary Lie subalgebra, yielding a four-mode spectrum and explicit projector and Euler–Cartan formulas. The abstract also states a normalized-Ricci-flow repeller separating collapse from the round basin, and rigidity and cut-locus results for deformed Cayley planes. paper.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
paper.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $\Sigma$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to \Sigma$ be a tubular neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $\Sigma$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $\Sigma$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$. In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $\Sigma$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus \Sigma$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $\Sigma$.

analysis.tldr: Under scalability assumptions, leaf-preserving diffeomorphisms can be isotoped to bundle morphisms near a singular leaf submanifold.
analysis.problem: Reduce homotopy-type questions for leaf-preserving diffeomorphism groups near singularities.
analysis.main_result: For a foliation with a singular submanifold and a tubular neighborhood, certain scalability assumptions imply that every leaf-preserving diffeomorphism is leaf-preservingly isotopic to one agreeing with a vector-bundle morphism near the submanifold. The result has foliated, compactly supported and parametrized forms and reduces group homotopy questions to diffeomorphisms of the singular submanifold, leaf-preserving bundle isomorphisms and diffeomorphisms supported away from the singularity. analysis.context: Foliation-preserving transformation groups.

paper.title: On $q$-real and $q$-complex numbers
paper.abstract: In arXiv:1812.00170 and arXiv:1908.04365, Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko introduced $q$-rational numbers $[x]_q$, rational functions specializing to $x$ at $q=1$, and their extension to $q$-real numbers, Laurent series agreeing with $[x]_q$ for rational $x$. It was conjectured in arXiv:2102.00891 that for every real $x>1$, $[x]_q$ has positive radius of convergence, with optimal common radius $R_*=(3-\sqrt{5})/2$, attained at the golden ratio. We prove that $[x]_q$ converges to a nonvanishing holomorphic function for every real $x>1$ and $|q|<3-2\sqrt{2}$. The proof gives an expansion of $1/[x]_q$ as a $q$-adically convergent series of rational functions, converging absolutely and locally uniformly on an explicit region. It also defines a positive analytic function for $q\in(-R_*,1)$. Using arXiv:2405.15970, we further obtain convergence for $|q|<2-\sqrt{3}$. We compute $[x]_q$ explicitly for some transcendental $x$, including ${\rm cotan}(1)$ and $e$. We also establish sharp inequalities for numerators and denominators of $q$-rationals when $|q|=1$ and determine the closure of the set of $[x]_q$ when such $q$ is not a root of unity. Next, we show that coefficientwise reduction modulo every $m\ge2$ is injective on the Cantor line (the extended real line with doubled up rationals and the Cantor set topology); for $m=2$, it identifies the Cantor line with $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_2((q)))$. We describe the inverse map, extend rationality results modulo every prime, characterize quadratic series over $\mathbb F_2(q)$ corresponding to quadratic irrationals, derive criteria for eventual parity of coefficients, and compute the real numbers corresponding to $1+q^n$. Finally, we propose a definition of $q$-complex number $[\tau]_q$, a meromorphic function in $\tau\in\mathbb C_+$ expressed via hypergeometric functions evaluated at modular functions of $\tau$.

Coefficient reduction modulo every integer at least two is injective on the Cantor line, and modulo two identifies it with \(\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_2((q)))\). paper.title: Generic classification of the quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_2$
paper.abstract: In this article we show that the quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_2$ are generically classifiable by the inverse temperature of their unique KMS state. Along the way, we show that a large class of quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_n$ are generically equivariantly $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and their corresponding dual action has the Rokhlin property generically.

A large class of quasi-free flows on \(\mathcal O_n\) is generically equivariantly \(\mathcal Z\)-stable, and its dual action generically has the Rokhlin property. paper.title: Global Analytical Solution of the Identical Kuramoto Model for N=3 via Koopman Eigenfunctions
paper.abstract: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic model of collective synchronization in coupled oscillator systems. Although its mathematical properties have been extensively investigated, explicit phase trajectories from arbitrary initial conditions have been available only for the simplest case, N = 2. In this study, we provide a global analytical solution for the phase trajectories of the all-to-all coupled Kuramoto model with three identical oscillators (N = 3). We construct Koopman eigenfunctions from products of observables whose growth rates, weighted by the exponents, sum to a constant, and obtain a nontrivial constant of motion from the ratio of two such eigenfunctions. Using their explicit exponential time dependence, we reduce trajectory reconstruction to time-dependent quartic equations and recover the phase trajectories. The same construction also yields Koopman eigenfunctions for the Kuramoto-Sakaguchi model with arbitrary phase lag and for the N = 4 all-to-all and ring-coupled systems. These results provide a concrete example in which Koopman eigenfunctions are used not only to characterize but also to explicitly solve a widely studied nonlinear model.

analysis.relevance_note: Koopman eigenfunctions and exact nonlinear trajectories provide an operator-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: Koopman eigenfunctions reduce the three-identical-oscillator Kuramoto trajectories to time-dependent quartics.
analysis.problem: Recover global phase trajectories of the all-to-all identical three-oscillator model.
analysis.main_result: The author constructs Koopman eigenfunctions from products of observables with weighted growth rates summing to a constant. Their ratio gives a nontrivial constant of motion, and explicit exponential evolution reduces trajectory recovery to time-dependent quartic equations. Related eigenfunctions are also constructed for Kuramoto–Sakaguchi with arbitrary phase lag and for four-oscillator all-to-all and ring coupling; a complete trajectory solution is claimed here for the identical three-oscillator case.
analysis.context: Koopman representations of coupled-oscillator dynamics.

paper.title: Attention as In-Context Empirical Bayes: A Two-Stage View via Particle Dynamics
paper.abstract: We study minimal attention-only transformers under all-token corruption and show they admit a two-stage empirical Bayes interpretation. A single attention step computes a kernel-weighted posterior mean with respect to the empirical distribution defined by the context. Depth refines this distribution through particle dynamics (Stage 1), while a long-range skip-connection carries the noisy input as a query for posterior inference (Stage 2), revealing distinct statistical roles for depth and attention residuals. The framework isolates a minimal setting in which the context itself induces a depth-dependent energy landscape governing in-context inference. We show that effective denoising can emerge without an explicit noise schedule: a fixed kernel bandwidth and finite integration horizon suffice, yielding a principled depth-noise relationship. We further establish a posterior-mean recovery guarantee for Gaussian priors, showing the empirical estimator converges to the Bayes-optimal predictor under sequential asymptotic conditions. Connecting these dynamics to reverse-diffusion limits, our results provide a statistical interpretation of attention as in-context inference via sample-based posterior estimation, without explicit density modeling.

paper.title: A criterion for weighted uniform distribution along functions from a Hardy field
paper.abstract: A classical theorem of Boshernitzan states that if $f$ is a function which belongs to a Hardy field and which satisfies $|f(x)|\prec x^{\ell}$ for some $\ell\in \mathbb{N}$, then the sequence $(f(n))_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is uniformly distributed modulo 1 if and only if $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{|f(x)-p(x)|}{\log(x)} = \infty$ for all $p(x)\in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. We provide a new proof of this result using methods from summability theory and we extend Boshernitzan's criterion by obtaining necessary and sufficient conditions for $f$ to be uniformly distributed modulo 1 with respect to a broad class of weighted averages. As an application of our results, we show that for the function $f(x) = x^{3/2}$ and for any $(a,b)\subset [0,1]$, and all sufficiently large $N\in\mathbb{N}$, there is an $n\in [N-N^{\frac{1}{4}},N]$ such that $f(n)\mod 1\in (a,b)$.

paper.title: Uniform Exponential Stability Analysis of Impulsive Linear Time-Invariant Systems on Banach and Hilbert Spaces: Non-Coercive and Coercive Stability Conditions
paper.abstract: We consider the uniform exponential stability analysis of infinite-dimensional impulsive systems defined on a Banach or Hilbert space, whose flow is governed by a fixed $C_0$-semigroup generator and whose jumps occur at a prescribed time sequence. While the flow and jump maps are themselves time-invariant, the time-triggered impulses render the propagator a genuinely time-varying evolution family, which is the source of the analysis difficulty addressed here. We combine ideas from hybrid systems theory and infinite-dimensional systems to produce operator-based stability conditions, which can be analytically or numerically checked via convex programming. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform exponential stability of impulsive systems on Banach spaces are obtained in the context of a fixed impulse-times sequence but also of arbitrary, constant, minimum, and range dwell-times using both non-coercive and coercive Lyapunov functionals. Some of those results are then adapted to systems on a Hilbert space and quadratic Lyapunov functionals. As an application, linear switched systems are shown to be an exact special case: reformulated as impulsive systems with unit-norm selector jumps, they inherit non-coercive and clock-dependent dwell-time stability conditions on both Banach and Hilbert spaces. Theoretical and numerical examples are given for illustration, notably on the sampled-data control of time-delay systems.
